samples.summary: Empty-children guard also drops legitimately-empty groups, conflicting with the doc's round-trip acceptance bar
samples.evidence: `if (!children) return '';` fires not only when children serialized away (dropped images / Phase-2 charts) but also when `data.children` is genuinely `[]`. The importer explicitly supports that case: `parseGrpSp` (packages/slides/src/import/pptx/shape.ts:197-247 — "Empty group fallback: if there are no children, fall back to the `<a:off>/<a:ext>` frame") produces a `GroupElement` with `children: []` and a `refSize`. `docs/design/slides/slides-pptx-export.md` §6 defines success as `import → export → re-import` deep-equal on a normalized projection over chart-free fixtures, with only the enumerated normalizations excluded; an imported empty group now silently disappears on export, so the model-equivalence criterion no longer holds for that shape of input and the loss is not listed in §6's "known importer loss" projection. If the empty group truly cannot be represented, the exclusion belongs in §6 (or the guard should distinguish "had children, all dropped" from "had no children").

samples.summary: New cascading element-drop rule is not recorded in the canonical PPTX-export design doc
samples.evidence: The doc enumerates every case where an element vanishes on export: Non-Goals say chart serialization "emits nothing so a chart is silently dropped", and §7 documents `onImageError` opting the CLI into dropping an unfetchable image. This delta adds a third, transitive rule — a whole `<p:grpSp>` (and, recursively, its ancestors) disappears when all of its descendants dropped — which is observable output behavior beyond the documented single-element drops and beyond §4's Group row ("recurse"). Per CONTRIBUTING the canonical subsystem doc should absorb this (a sentence in Non-Goals/§4/§6), not just a code comment.

verdict.reason: Every claimed fact verified. group.ts:115-122 computes `children` by joining serialized children and returns '' when falsy — which includes a genuinely empty `data.children` array, not just the "all children dropped" case the comment at :117-121 reasons about. The importer reachably produces that state: parseGrpSp (shape.ts:200-259) returns undefined only when <a:xfrm> is missing (:207); with no children, combinedBoundingBox([]) is falsy (:217,:221), it falls back to the <a:off>/<a:ext> frame (:222-226) and builds a GroupElement with children: [] and a refSize (:236-248), exactly as the "Empty group fallback" comment at :197-198 states. Nothing in import/pptx prunes empty groups. The model invariant "a group has at least one child" (docs/design/slides/slides-group.md:130) is explicitly scoped to store enforcement via memory.ts group(), which the importer bypasses, and model/group.ts:275-293 tolerates the empty case defensively — so no guard makes this unreachable. slides-pptx-export.md:228-254 sets the acceptance bar as normalize(reimport) deep-equal to normalize(import) with exactly four enumerated exclusions; an exporter-side deletion of an empty group is not "known importer loss" and is not otherwise listed, while the comparable chart omission IS explicitly documented (doc:22, :62-63), showing the doc's convention. In lane: this is an unmet §6 acceptance criterion plus an undocumented deviation from the design doc, which the rubric classes as major, not a line-level logic bug. No named refutation ground applies.
